description: Work a story test-first: understand it, write the failing test, implement to green, verify, self-review, commit, close out.

story.description: the story bead this formula works

kind.description: 'bug' when the story is a bug (its type is bug or its title starts '[bug]'), otherwise 'feature'; mw next sets it

steps.title: Understand {{story}}: {{title}}
steps.description: Read the story bead {{story}}'s description and acceptance criteria, and read the code it touches, before changing anything.

steps.title: Write the failing feature or test first
steps.description: Write the Gherkin feature or unit test that captures {{story}}'s acceptance criteria, and confirm it fails for the right reason.

steps.title: Write the regression test from his report, and see it fail
steps.description: Write the regression test for {{story}} from his report first: the screen, the words, the steps he gave. Run it on this branch before any fix and see it fail for the reason he saw. If it cannot fail (the fake hides it), say so on the bead and make the fake honest enough to fail, then run it again. Do not go on until you have seen it fail for his reason.

steps.title: Implement until green
steps.description: Write the implementation for {{story}} until the failing test or feature from the previous step passes.

steps.title: Run the full build, tests and vet
steps.description: Run the rig's build, the full test suite and vet; all must pass clean, not just the new test. Run the gate in the foreground, under the Bash tool's own timeout: `timeout 590 make test`, then `make lint`; or `mw check {{story}}`, which makes the checks mw next makes. If mw check {{story}} names parts of the gate that have not been run (this rig's gate is split into parts because the whole of it outruns a tool call), run `mw check {{story}} --part N` for each part, one per Bash call and each in the foreground, then `mw check {{story}}` with no part: it runs none of the gate and reports the whole gate green, or the parts that failed or were not run at this commit. Never nohup or background it and wait with tail --pid, a sleep loop or polling: the auto-mode classifier refuses that wait and the story stops with its steps open. If the foreground run times out, say so on the bead and hand back. If `mw check {{story}} --part N` ends with one line saying the merge slot is held and the part did not start, run that part once more; if the line comes again, do not start a background loop: comment on the bead naming each part not yet run and the command `mw check {{story}} --part N` that runs it, and hand back, and mw next will name those parts again in its mail. A check 'under load' runs under contrib/mw-under-load <command>; never hand-rolled busy loops, stress or yes on a host.

steps.title: Self-review the diff against the acceptance criteria
steps.description: Read the whole diff for {{story}} end to end against its acceptance criteria before committing.

steps.title: Commit
steps.description: Commit the change for {{story}} in small, plainly described commits, with no AI attribution lines.

steps.title: Write the closing comment and propose rig memory notes
steps.description: Comment on {{story}} with what was built, what was verified and how, and anything left undone. When your diff adds or changes a file under grinds/examples/ (grinds/examples/<kind>/<name>.json), run each such example against the live mill first (`mw grist eval <app> <kind> --example <name>`, with `--ref` your branch) and write a line for it in the comment, 'mw grist eval <app> <kind> --example <name>: PASS': the fake mill is not proof, and a close-out refuses a comment with no such line for an example the branch changed. Before that section, when the story changes something the Governor can see, add a section headed exactly 'HOW TO CHECK IT, for the Governor': at most six plain numbered steps with the exact on-screen labels and what right looks like. Quote every label from the source, never from memory: find it in the component (grep the rig's src/ for it), put it between double quotes, and quote nothing you did not find there. After you comment, run `mw lint-checkit {{story}} --dir .`: it exits non-zero and names each quoted label not found in src/, and then you comment again with the corrected section (the newest HOW TO CHECK IT is the one read); otherwise write the single line 'Internal: nothing for the Governor to look at'. Also give one line, 'What's new: New: <one plain sentence the Governor would understand, no file names>' or 'What's new: Fixed: <one plain sentence, no file names>', or 'What's new: none' for a change he cannot see (tests, docs, internal): mw next writes it into the app's changelog when the rig keeps one. END the closing comment with a section headed exactly 'For the rig memory:' holding at most two typed facts that a later Builder on this rig would have been saved real time by, one per line, each written as the ready mw memory command that places it (write it, never run it): `mw memory add <rig> --kind gotcha|decision --subject <subject> --source {{story}} "<sentence>"`, `mw memory supersede <rig> <slug> --source {{story}} "<sentence>"`, `mw memory retire <rig> <slug> --reason "<reason>"` or `mw memory recheck <rig> <slug> --why "<why>"` (a slug names a fact the rig memory already holds; add `--slug <name>` to an add or a supersede to name the new fact), or the single word 'nothing'. mw next passes each line to the Mayor as that command with the story as its source, and flags a line it cannot read; the older forms 'gotcha [subject]: <sentence>' and 'retire <slug>: <reason>' are still read. The Builder does NOT edit the rig memory file: the Mayor places what he keeps.
